desc:
The string s is the binary representation of a positive integer. Repeat the following until the number equals 1, and return how many steps are needed:

  • If the number is even, divide it by 2.
  • If the number is odd, add 1 to it.

The number can have thousands of bits, so you cannot convert it to a machine integer.

Example: "1101" is 13. The sequence is 13, 14, 7, 8, 4, 2, 1, which takes 6 steps. Example: "10" takes 1 step; "1" takes 0.
constraints: s contains only 0 and 1 and starts with 1
hints: Dividing an even number by 2 removes its last bit (a 0). Adding 1 to an odd number turns trailing ones into zeros and creates a carry.
Process the bits from the right, keeping a carry that says whether a +1 has already been pushed into the current bit.

Look at bit + carry: if it is 1 (the number is odd) you need 2 steps (add 1, then divide) and the carry becomes 1; if it is 0 or 2 (even) you need 1 step (divide), and the carry is 1 only for 2. Do this for every bit except the leading one, then add the final carry.
editorial: Simulating the process on a big integer would be quadratic. Instead, look at the number from its lowest bit. Every bit except the leading one has to be removed by a division, which costs 1 step. An odd value in the lowest position additionally costs an add-one step, and that addition changes the number: it flips the trailing ones to zeros and carries into the next bit.

Track this with a carry. Going from the second-to-last bit down to bit 1 (the leading bit at index 0 stays), compute v = bit + carry. If v == 1 the current lowest bit is odd: spend 2 steps and the carry stays 1. If v == 0 spend 1 step and the carry is 0. If v == 2 the bit is effectively 0 with a carry: spend 1 step and keep carry 1. When only the leading 1 remains, a pending carry means the value is 2, which needs one more step. So the answer is the step count plus the carry. One pass, O(n).
